source.check: Returning Officer's Notice of Result (Ulster Herald, 11 June 1949, p. 2), no poll in this division; read from the INA page OCR, where the surname and other-names columns are separate runs aligned here by row order (INA page images need a subscription). note: Triennial election of the electoral divisions of Omagh rural district, one member each, polled on 2 June 1949. For the first time in 25 years four divisions were contested (Bencran, Gortin, Maine, Moyle), three by Anti-Partitionists and one by an Independent, all against Unionists. 'Seventeen Unionists and seventeen Anti-Partitionists were returned unopposed, but in one Nationalist division no nomination was received and the retiring member will be deemed re-elected'; four new members came in unopposed (Ulster Herald, 21 May 1949, p. 5). The unopposed members are recorded from the Returning Officer's Notice of Result (Ulster Herald, 11 June 1949, p. 2), read from the page OCR. Tattymoyle has no candidate in the notice's name columns; its column 6 names the retiring councillor, Peter Connolly, as re-elected (read on the block image, 7 Nov 2026). Returned unopposed.
correctionNote: Renamed from 'Rahoney' to Rahony (19 Nov 2026, w19-merges, the owner's decision 4 of 19 Nov 2026: a division filed under two spellings takes its official DED name, and each round keeps the spelling it was filed under as Constituency_Name_As_Printed): the NI DED maps of 1925-39 name Omagh Rural District's DED Rahony, as the 1927 round is filed. This round was filed as 'Rahoney', the spelling of its source, kept as Constituency_Name_As_Printed; the old address (rahoney) answers with a redirect to this one.
